cards.front: What does LVRT require of a wind plant?
cards.back: Stay connected while the voltage stays above the grid code's LVRT curve.

cards.front: Why do grid codes require fault ride-through?
cards.back: Mass disconnection during faults would turn a small fault into a large loss of generation.

cards.front: How is reactive current during a dip usually set?
cards.back: A gain K times the voltage deviation, up to the converter current limit.

cards.front: What does a voltage-dip container use to create the dip?
cards.back: An impedance divider: series impedance plus a switched shunt impedance at the turbine terminals.

cards.front: When is a simulation accepted as compliance evidence?
cards.back: Only when the model has been validated against field measurements.

cards.front: Name two common plotting mistakes in FRT reports.
cards.back: Using the wrong per-unit base, and checking only the depth of the dip but not its duration.

cards.front: Why do weak grids worry converter control?
cards.back: Voltage swings more with power changes, so control loops can become unstable.

cards.front: Where is reactive capability checked for compliance?
cards.back: At the point of interconnection (POI), including plant losses.

How is a reactive capability gap usually closed?
cards.back: With a STATCOM or a capacitor bank.

cards.front: What must the test report include?
cards.back: Raw data and plots for every test, not just a summary.
